content:
We have carbon NMR data with many peaks. Aromatic carbons typically appear ~110-160 ppm. The list: 166.00 (likely carbonyl), 151.10, 144.35, 140.45, 137.05, 131.30 (two same), 124.40, 122.30, 119.00, 116.65 (two). Those in aromatic region: 151.10,144.35,140.45,137.05,131.30,131.30,124.40,122.30,119.00,116.65,116.65. That's 11 peaks. However aromatic carbons may be duplicated due to symmetry; count of aromatic carbons in molecule is number of aromatic carbon atoms, not distinct chemical shifts. Need to infer from molecule? Could be a benzene ring (6) plus maybe heteroaromatic? The carbon NMR shows many aromatic signals, maybe a naphthalene (10) plus carbonyl etc. 11 aromatic signals suggests maybe 11 aromatic carbons (some may be quaternary). Could be a phenyl plus pyridine? But we don't have structure.

We could get HSQC to map protons to carbons, but we just need count of aromatic carbons. Could also use proton NMR to see aromatic protons count. Let's get proton NMR.
